parameters.description: The custom entry id (without the `custom:` prefix)

404.description: No custom entry with that id

put.summary: Hide or un-hide one library title.
put.description:
Curation, not access control: the title leaves every play surface and launch resolution
but is not deleted. The operator console still lists it (`hidden: true`) so it can return.
The id is not required to exist now — a plugin mid-sync or an unmounted drive would
otherwise refuse a choice that should stick. Emits `library.changed` only on a real change.

200.description: Stored; the entry's visibility after the call

put.description:
The payload is the desired set, keyed by `external_id`. The host diffs, keeps surviving
host ids stable, and drops orphans. Empty array removes everything this provider owns.
Emits `library.changed` with the provider as `source`.

`?store=` claims that store: entries surface as `<store>:<external_id>` with the store
badge. One provider per store; a second claimant gets 409. Release the claim with
`DELETE`, not an empty reconcile — a store can have zero installed titles.

parameters.name: store
parameters.description: Claim this store for the provider ([a-z0-9_-], `custom`/`manual` reserved)

200.description: The provider's resulting entries (host ids assigned/kept)

400.description: Invalid provider id, store id, or payload

409.description: That store is already claimed by another provider

delete.description:
Everything owned by `{provider}`, for plugin uninstall. Emits `library.changed`
when anything was removed.

put.summary: Report which of a provider's titles are running.
put.description:
Live counterpart to reconcile `detect` hints: the body is the complete running set
([`crate::runstate`]). Missed events and plugin restarts self-correct on the next PUT.

Authoritative for [`crate::runstate::REPORT_TTL`] unless restated; a dead plugin then
falls back to process scanning. Re-report on change and on a timer inside the window.
Titles the provider does not currently publish count as `unknown`, not an error — a
report may race its own reconcile.

get.description:
One row per installed library plugin, with its enable state. Sources default to
enabled; disabling hides titles from the next read. The custom store is not a
source and is always on. Every row is
`origin: "plugin"`.

200.description: This host's scanners with their enable state

put.summary: Enable or disable a library source.
put.description:
Takes effect on the next library read. Disabling hides titles; the plugin may keep
reconciling while off. Nothing is deleted. Emits `library.changed` when the state changes.

200.description: Toggle stored; the full scanner list

404.description: No such scanner on this platform

get.description: Unauthenticated; `require_auth` admits loopback only.

200.description: Non-sensitive local host status (loopback peers only)

get.description:
In-memory, DEBUG and above, independent of `RUST_LOG`. Poll with `after` = last
`next`. `dropped: true` means the ring wrapped between polls and entries were
evicted.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return entries with seq greater than this (omitted/0 = oldest retained)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max entries per response (default and cap 1000)

200.description: Entries after the cursor, oldest first

delete.description:
One persisted write, not a loop (a mid-loop failure would half-empty the
store), and every live native session those clients own is stopped.
Idempotent, so 200 rather than the single unpair's 204/404: an empty store
still succeeds, and `unpaired` tells the operator what it meant.

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: Hex SHA-256 of the client certificate (case-insensitive)

404.description: No paired native client with that fingerprint

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: Hex SHA-256 of the client certificate (case-insensitive)

200.description: Access updated; the stored record as now in force

400.description: Reserved grant bits set, or expires_in_secs together with clear_expiry

404.description: No paired native client with that fingerprint

get.description:
Poll while armed to show the PIN and countdown. `enabled: false` means
GameStream only (no `--native`).

post.description:
Opens a window and mints a PIN. `grants` / `expires_in_secs` apply to
whichever device completes the ceremony.

200.description: Pairing armed; the response carries the PIN to display

503.description: Native host not available in this process

get.description:
Unpaired knocks while pairing is required. Approve to pair without a PIN.
Entries expire after ~10 minutes.

200.description: Devices awaiting approval (empty when none, or when the native host is not enabled)

post.description:
Pairs the fingerprint immediately (no PIN). `{}` keeps the knock name and
stored access (full/permanent on first pairing). The response is the stored
record, not necessarily this request's inputs.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Pending-request id from the pending list

200.description: Device paired; the stored record as now in force

404.description: No pending request with that id (expired?)

409.description: Knock came from the internet; arm a fingerprint-bound PIN instead

post.description: Drops the request. Not a blocklist — the next attempt knocks again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Pending-request id from the pending list

404.description: No pending request with that id

get.description: Poll this to know when to prompt for the PIN Moonlight displays.

200.description: Whether a pairing handshake is waiting for a PIN

post.description: Completes the out-of-band half of the handshake.

204.description: PIN delivered to the waiting handshake

400.description: Malformed PIN or unparseable JSON body

409.description: No pairing handshake is waiting for a PIN

422.description: JSON body does not match the schema

get.description: Live, secret-free directory. The console fetches the secret separately, server-side.

post.description:
Plugins are not host children — their output never hits the host `tracing` subscriber. Lines
share the host ring as `plugin:<source>` so `GET /logs` needs no second cursor.

put.description:
Idempotent lease renew (~30 s). Emits `plugins.changed` only when an operator-visible field
changed; a pure renewal is silent.

delete.description:
Immediate remove (SDK finalizer on SIGTERM). Emits `plugins.changed` only for a live entry;
unknown/expired is a silent 204.

get.summary: Fetch a plugin UI's proxy credential
get.description:
Server-side `{port, secret}` for the console proxy. The console BFF denylists this from the
browser.

404.description: No live plugin with that id, or it serves no UI

delete.description: A deliberate stop: skip keep-alive linger and apply `game_on_session_end`.

get.description:
What each session came to — mode, codec, bitrate, frames, bring-up, and why it ended
— newest first, at most the last eight. This is the whole of what the host knows, so
the answer is what a bug report should carry.

A host that has not streamed since it started answers with an empty list.

200.description: Finished sessions, newest first; empty if none
Stored settings + which axes this build enforces

put.description:
Persisted clamped. Takes effect on the next decision, including a session
already streaming — policy is read at session end, not start.

delete.description:
Same deliberate stop as `DELETE /session`, for the one id. Every other live
session keeps streaming.

404.description: No live session with that id

put.description:
Re-points the LIVE grant set — the mask the input thread already checks every
event against — so a guest gets the pad, or loses it, without reconnecting.
The pairing's stored access is untouched, and a later edit to it wins.

The ceiling is the pairing's own mask: what is asked for is ANDed with it, so this
route can narrow or restore, never grant a device something it was not paired for.
The applied mask comes back, which is how a caller sees the clamp.

200.description: Applied mask, after the pairing clamp

400.description: No level or grants, an unknown level, or reserved bits

404.description: No live session with that id

put.description:
Drops this session's audio at the wire, nothing else: the capturer and the sink
stay up, so a session sharing the display keeps hearing. The client is told, so
its overlay can name the silence instead of the player guessing.

404.description: No live session with that id

post.summary: Request a keyframe on one session

404.description: No live session with that id

get.description:
One frame per pad state the host applies — what it injects, not what the client
says it sent — so a controller question is answered from the host's own hand
instead of an evdev dump. `data:` is a [`PadFrame`]; `event:` is `pad.state`.
Attaching replays every live pad, so a button already held draws at once.

Console lane only, like the window routes: a paired certificate is not bound to
a session id, and this is the operator's own machine watching its own input.

Nothing is published while nobody is attached, so a console on another page —
or none at all — costs the input thread one atomic load per pad event.

200.description: SSE stream; each frame's `data:` is one PadFrame

404.description: No live session with that id

503.description: Concurrent event-stream cap reached — retry shortly

put.description:
Which controller this session is: slot 0 is Player 1, and a local co-op game
reads that order. Without a pick the slot is whichever comes free, so the pad
that moves first takes Player 1 and the order changes on every reconnect.

The pick is a reservation, not a seizure. A pad already built keeps the slot it
was created under until it re-plugs; a slot another live session asked for first
stays theirs and this call answers `reserved: false`. It is remembered against
the device's pairing, so the same device reconnects as the same player — an
anonymous session's pick lasts only as long as the session.

200.description: The pick, and whether it took the slot

400.description: Slot past the host's pad count

404.description: No live session with that id

get.description:
The toplevels on the head this session streams, so a client in a full-screen
game can see what is behind it. Free to every session: those windows are
already in the pixels it receives. The operator's other monitors are not in
the payload, whatever the caller's access.

404.description: No live session with that id

post.summary: Act on one of this session's windows
post.description:
Focus, full-screen or close by id, gated on the session's LIVE grants — the
same mask the input thread checks every event against. A view-only guest is
refused all three; a controller-only guest raises a window but never closes
one. An id this session's head does not currently hold is a 404, so a stale
id cannot act on whatever now answers to it.

403.description: This session's access does not cover the verb

404.description: No such session, or no such window on its head

200.description: The in-progress capture (meta + samples so far)

404.description: No capture is currently recording

post.summary: Arm a capture. Idempotent if one is already running.
post.description:
Streaming loops emit aggregated samples every 1–2 s into the in-progress
capture (`GET /stats/capture/live`).

200.description: In-progress capture status (idle when not armed)

post.summary: Disarm and write the capture to disk atomically.

get.description: Summaries only (`meta`, no sample body), newest first.

404.description: No recording with that id
No recording with that id

200.description: Streaming/pairing state and the active session, if any

get.description:
Merged view across sources, annotated with what this host has and can run. A source past its
freshness window is refreshed first; a miss keeps the last copy marked `stale` — the pin
travelled with the entry.

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token

post.description:
`{source, id}` installs the catalog pin after re-checking integrity, or `{spec,
accept_unverified: true}` installs unreviewed code the operator owns. `202` + job id; watch at
`GET /store/jobs/{id}`.

One package operation at a time (`409` otherwise): `bun` shares a lockfile and `node_modules`.

400.description: Unknown entry, bad spec, or missing acknowledgement

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token

409.description: Another package operation is in flight

get.description:
Plugins-dir packages, with provenance and live registration. No provenance record means CLI
install (`tier: "cli"`); absence is the answer, not a gap.

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token
Not authorized for the plugin token

get.description: Poll this while `state` is `running`; `log` carries the tail of the package manager's output.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The job id returned by install/uninstall

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token

404.description: No such job (they are kept for a bounded history)

post.description: Bypasses the freshness window, re-fetches all sources, returns the merged catalog.

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token

get.description:
Plugins run only while the runner is on. The runner discovers units at startup, so a freshly
installed plugin may not have appeared yet.

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token

post.summary: Turn the plugin runner on or off

400.description: The runner could not be switched

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token
Not authorized for the plugin token

put.summary: Add or update a catalog source
put.description:
Its entries become installable and attributed to it. They never carry `verified`; that badge is
the built-in source alone.

400.description: Invalid name, url or key — or the reserved built-in name

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token
The built-in source cannot be removed, or the plugin token is not authorized

post.description:
Drops the package and its provenance, then restarts the runner. Only names the runner would
supervise: a shared dependency cannot be ripped out of the tree.

403.description: Not authorized for the plugin token

409.description: Another package operation is in flight

post.description:
Only for install kinds that support it. No version or URL in the body — the host
installs the verified manifest. Poll `GET /update/status` (`job`); after restart,
the outcome is `last_result`.

409.description: Refused: unsupported install kind, apply disabled (PUNKTFUNK_UPDATE_APPLY=0), a job already running, an active streaming session without `force`, or nothing newer to apply

post.summary: Force a manifest fetch and verification.
post.description:
One forced check per 30 s. `last_error` is a failed check; `not_published`
is an empty channel, not a failure.

200.description: Refreshed update-check state (`last_error` carries a failed check; `not_published` an empty channel, which is not one)

409.description: Update checks are disabled on this host

429.description: A forced check ran less than 30 s ago

get.description:
A cache older than 6 h may kick a background refresh. The response never
blocks on the network.

get.summary: Where to reach the browser plane

200.description: The live certificate hash and port

404.description: The browser plane is not enabled on this host

ActionInfo.description: One action as the caller sees it (`GET /actions`).

available.description: Platform probe. A VM that cannot S3 lists sleep as unavailable rather than a dead switch.

id.description: Invoke path parameter (`power.sleep`, …).

permitted.description: Whether THIS caller may invoke it (admin: always; cert: live `GRANT_POWER` bit).

title.description: Clients localize known ids and fall back to this for unknown ones.

app_id.description: Store-qualified library id (`steam:570`); matches `GET /library`. Absent for a typed GameStream command.

awaiting_window.description:
Present and true while `running` on a host that will report `window` next. A launch hold
waits for that instead of revealing a game that is still loading.

client.description: Client-supplied device name of the session that launched it; may be empty.

grace_remaining_s.description: Seconds until this game is ended — only present on a `grace` row.

session_id.description:
Streaming session; `null` while waiting out the reconnect window. Pass it to
`DELETE /session/{id}` to stop that one session.

state.description:
`launching` | `running` | `window` (its window is on the streamed screen) | `exited` |
`untracked` (exit will never be seen) | `grace` (reconnect window).

store.description: Which store surfaced it (`steam`, `heroic`, `custom`, …), when known.

ApiActiveGpu.description: GPU live encode sessions are on now (not the next-session pick).

id.description: Matches a `gpus` entry; empty when encoding on CPU/software.

ApiCodec.description: Wire token is the stack's canonical codec name (`Codec::label`). `H265` serializes as `"hevc"`, not `"h265"`.

ApiDisplayInfo.description: One live or kept virtual display.

display_index.description: Ordinal within the group, acquire order, 0-based.

expires_in_ms.description: Milliseconds until a lingering display is torn down (absent when active/pinned).

group.description: Shared-desktop group id; same group = one desktop.

identity_slot.description: Per-client identity slot (absent = shared/anonymous). Keys persistent config and manual layout.

ApiGpu.description: Hardware GPU. Software/WARP adapters are never listed.

id.description: `vendorid-deviceid-occurrence` (hex PCI). Stable across reboot/driver; not an index or LUID.

vram_mb.description: 0 when the platform does not expose dedicated VRAM.

ApiMonitorInfo.description: Physical monitor as the compositor reports it.

description.description: Picker label (`make model`, else the connector).

enabled.description: Driven right now. Disabled heads stay listed so they are not missing from the picker.

managed.description: Best-effort: one of our virtual displays, not a real head. Reliable on KWin only.

mode.description: `WIDTHxHEIGHT@HZ` of the current mode (size only when the refresh is unknown).

selected.description: True when `PUNKTFUNK_CAPTURE_MONITOR` currently names this monitor.

x.description: Desktop-space top-left. Distinguishes two heads of the same size.

ApiSelectedGpu.description: GPU the next session opens on. A running session keeps the GPU it already opened.

force.description: Apply even with a live stream (the stream drops when the host restarts).

ApprovePending.description:
Approve body. `{}` keeps the knock name and, on re-approve, stored access
(full/permanent on a first pairing).

expires_in_secs.description:
Access lifetime from now, seconds. Host stores the absolute deadline.
Alone: full control until then.

grants.description:
Grant mask. Reserved bits are 400. Omit both access fields to keep
stored access; `grants` alone is permanent.

name.description: Label; defaults to the name the device knocked with.

until_disconnect.description:
Drop the device's record once its last session ends, rather than at a clock time.
Combines with `expires_in_secs`: whichever comes first ends the grant. Send it with an
access level, never alone (400) — like the other access fields it is part of a whole
replacement, so sending `grants` without it clears it.

expires_in_secs.description:
Access lifetime from now, seconds — not `ttl_secs`. Host stores the
absolute deadline. Omit for permanent (`grants` set) or preserved (neither).

fingerprint.description:
Hex SHA-256 fingerprint that may consume this window. Omit for any
device (trusted-LAN only).

grants.description:
Grant mask for the device that completes the window. Reserved bits are
400. Omit both access fields for full (new) or preserved (re-pair).

ttl_secs.description: Window length, seconds. Default 120; clamped to 15–600.

until_disconnect.description:
Drop the device's record once its last session ends, rather than at a clock time.
Combines with `expires_in_secs`: whichever comes first ends the grant. Send it with an
access level, never alone (400) — like the other access fields it is part of a whole
replacement, so sending `grants` without it clears it.

Artwork.description:
Cover art. The client prefers `portrait` for a grid and falls back to `header`
when a title has no 600×900 capsule (common for older Steam apps).

AudioEgress.description: Audio egress for the whole session. Absent when the session had no audio plane.

infilled.description: Frames synthesized over a capture hole. Wire continuity is not captured continuity.

late.description: Departures a whole frame or more behind their slot.

reanchors.description: Times the pacer fell far enough behind to forgive its debt and re-anchor.

AudioPolicy.description:
Audio while this title runs: which of the sessions on its display hear it.
`all` is the same as no policy and is stored as none.

AudioSessions.description: Which sessions hear a title's audio (`audio.sessions` on a custom entry).

AudioWiring.description: Windows audio wiring: which endpoint carries each role. Names are the Sound-settings friendly names.

last_resort.description: Loopback is the degraded last resort; desktop audio may be silent until endpoints change.

loopback.description: Desktop-audio loopback friendly name; absent = unavailable.

mic.description: Virtual-mic write-target friendly name; absent = unavailable.

mic_withheld.description: Mic withheld so game audio keeps the only working sink.

narrowing.description: Why the chosen loopback endpoint NARROWS the desktop mix (rate/channels), when it does.

AvailableCompositor.description: A compositor backend and whether it is usable now.

available.description: Usable now: the live session's compositor, or gamescope if its binary is installed.

default.description: True for the backend an `Auto` (unspecified) request resolves to right now.

id.description: Stable id (`kwin` | `wlroots` | `mutter` | `gamescope`); pass to `--compositor`.

BitrateSpan.description: What the encoder's target did over the session. Absent when no encoder opened.

adaptive_steps.description:
Times the target moved after the opening rate: adaptive-bitrate decisions, plus a
rebuild re-resolving what it actually encodes.

avg_kbps.description:
Mean of the targets the session ran at, NOT weighted by how long each held.
A rate held for a second counts as much as one held for an hour.

Capture.description: Wire and on-disk shape: summary plus sample time-series.

link.description:
One row per minute of link health per native session, so a freeze report carries the
loss, recovery and ABR history instead of a log ring that holds 45 minutes. Empty on a
GameStream capture and on recordings older than this field.

stages.description: The rungs run, in ladder order.

CaptureHealth.description:
Per-session capture health (Windows IDD-push): the live classifier verdict, the driver
encoder's self-report and the last staged-recovery episode.

backend_opened.description: The backend the driver opened: `nvenc` / `amf` / `qsv` / `pyrowave`. Absent as above.

cooldown_remaining_ms.description: Time left in the post-failure cooldown, while one is in force.

current_stage.description: The recovery stage running now, while an episode is open.

detached.description: Encode threads the driver abandoned after a wedge; two opens the driver cycle.

encoder_state.description:
The driver encoder's own state word: `closed` / `open` / `encoding` / `wedged`.
Absent until the session's first `SET_ENCODE`.

episodes_suppressed.description: Stalled verdicts refused for budget or cooldown since the last episode.

oneOf.description: The last closed recovery episode.

late_frames.description:
`present_to_arrival_ms` is past the classifier's bound: frames come late rather than not
at all. Reported only — no recovery rung fires on it.

present_to_arrival_ms.description: The newest access unit's OS present stamp against the moment the host took it.

published_total.description: Access units the driver published, and frames it dropped at its encode pool.

source_gap_ms.description: Time since the last real source frame.

CaptureMeta.description:
Filename stem plus negotiated mode/codec/client. On-disk head;
[`StatsRecorder::list`] returns this without the sample body.

encoder_backend.description:
Backend that actually opened (`"nvenc"`, `"vaapi"`, `"vulkan"`, `"amf"`,
`"qsv"`, `"software"`, …), from `pf_gpu::active()`. Stage timings are
unreadable without it. `""` if nothing was streaming at registration.

truncated.description: The sample cap was hit: samples past it were dropped and the start kept.

CaptureStage.description: One recovery rung of an episode.

blocked.description: Revocation of the catalogued version; listed, never offered quietly.

categories.description: Browse filters; the Game-sources add-rail is exactly the `library` entries.

detected.description:
Host-side existence probe for the launcher this plugin scans. `null` = no probe for this
platform (unknown, not "not installed").

reviewed_at.description: When unom reviewed this exact tarball (built-in source only).

tier.description:
`verified` (built-in) or `external` (operator-added). Never `unverified`: those come from a
raw spec and are not listed.

version.description: The one installable version this entry pins.

nonce.description: 32 random bytes, lowercase hex. Single-use, and short-lived.

CheckSource.description:
Origin of a verdict. `Event` is for live feeds (push on transition); v1 emits `Startup` and
`Refresh` only.

CheckStatus.description:
Probe result. `Inapplicable` is not `Ok`: "never on this box" and "works here" are different
answers on the troubleshooting page.

device_name.description: Paired device name at upload, filesystem-sanitized.

fingerprint_prefix.description:
First 16 hex chars of the pairing fingerprint — enough to match the roster
without repeating the full identity in every filename.

id.description: Filename stem; pass to fetch/delete.

received_ms.description: Upload time (unix ms from the file mtime, not the stem timestamp).

ClientOverlay.description:
One paired device's deviations from the host policy
(`design/web-console-overhaul.md` §6.1).

Every field is optional and absent means **follow the host**. That is the
whole point: a copied policy would silently stop following host changes,
while an overlay only pins what the operator actually chose for this
device. The TV wants take-over and keep-forever; the tablet wants its own
screen and no linger — one host policy cannot serve both.

`max_displays` and `layout` are deliberately absent: they are properties of
the host's desktop, not of a device connecting to it.

capture_monitor.description:
Mirror this connector for this device only. Absent follows the host,
which is also the only way back to a virtual screen — a device cannot
opt OUT of a host-wide pin. Nobody has asked to; the reverse direction
is what the field exists for.

max_mode.description:
Largest mode this device is granted, `WIDTHxHEIGHT@HZ`. A phone asking for 4K120
on a weak host degrades every other session; the operator caps it once and the
client is told the smaller mode rather than silently given one.

scale.description:
Scale this device's screen is created at, when the desktop has not already
remembered one for it (`display-management.md` §5.4). Mutter mints a fresh EDID
serial per session, so its own `monitors.xml` never rematches — without this the
operator re-sets the scale on every connect.

name.description:
Display name: the trust-store name (a console rename wins), else the name the client
sent. On the compat plane it is the name the operator gave the device, since Moonlight
sends none. Empty when there is no name at all.

oneOf.description: Which sessions hear this title. Absent = every session.

detect.description:
How to find this title after a command that hands off and exits. Without it the
host tracks only the child it spawned.

external_id.description: Provider's reconcile key. Present iff `provider` is, so the host `id` can stay put.

icon.description: Brand token (`steam`, `heroic`) a client draws. Never bytes, never a URL. See [`GameEntry::icon`].

id.description: Host-assigned row id; the `{id}` in the CRUD path. Not the surfaced library id.

on_window.description:
Which workspace this title opens on ([`crate::library::OnWindow`]).
Absent follows the host's display policy.

prep.description: Each `do` runs before launch; each `undo` at session end in reverse ([`crate::hooks::run_prep`]).

provider.description:
Set only by provider reconcile. `None` is a manual row: reconcile never touches it, and
manual CRUD refuses provider-owned rows.

store.description:
Store this row was claimed under. `None` surfaces as `custom`. Stamped on the
row so id and badge stay correct while [`Catalog::claims`] is being rewritten.

CustomEntry.description: One stored row. Same shape the API returns and the console edits.

allOf.description: Flattened [`GameMeta`]. Replaced wholesale on update — an edit must send every field it wants kept.

oneOf.description: Absent on an update keeps the stored policy; `{"sessions":"all"}` clears it.
Absent on an update keeps the stored hint, as with `prep`.

icon.description: Brand token. A hand-added "Steam" tile can look like one. See [`GameEntry::icon`].

oneOf.description: Absent on an update keeps the stored placement, as with `prep`.

prep.description:
Run as the host user; operator-privileged. See [`privileged_field`]. Absent on an
update keeps the stored list: a writer that never read it must not clear it.

role.description: A hand-added launcher tile is legal without installing the matching plugin.

CustomInput.description: Create/replace body. No `id` — the host assigns it.

CustomPreset.description:
Operator-named bundle of the six axes plus game-session, stored in
`<config>/display-presets.json`. Applying one writes a `Custom`
[`DisplayPolicy`] via `PUT /display/settings`. Editing the catalog never
mutates the running policy; re-apply to adopt.

game_session.description: Unlike a built-in preset, applying a custom preset sets this axis.

id.description: Host-assigned, stable for the life of the entry.

CustomPresetInput.description: Create/replace body. No `id` — the host owns it.

DetectHint.description:
Inbound wire half of [`DetectSpec`]: what an operator or plugin can name about
recognizing a title. Every field optional; all empty is no hint.

Not returned by the catalog API — detect data does not go outbound.

steam_appid.description: Without this a Steam plugin degrades from reaper match to install-dir prefix.

checks.description:
Every registered check, worst-first, including `ok` and `inapplicable`. The console decides
what to hide.

DisconnectReason.description: `Quit` is the typed close; `Timeout` is transport idle; `Error` is everything else.

DisplayHealth.description: Host-wide Windows display health: the topology transaction log and the leases the stream holds.

driver_protocol.description: Protocol the installed pf-vdisplay driver answered at the last handshake; absent until a session ran one.

host_protocol.description: Protocol this host drives; a driver answering less fails every session.

oneOf.description: The most recent topology transaction, if any.

pnp_leases.description:
Monitor devnodes disabled for a stream and not yet re-enabled (a leftover here after a
crash is what the next host start replays).

topology_generation.description: Count of topology transactions that observed a change since the host started.

DisplayLayoutRequest.description: Manual layout: identity-slot id as string (same id `/display/state` reports) → desktop offset.

DisplayPolicy.description:
File + mgmt GET/PUT shape. When [`preset`](Self::preset) is not
[`Preset::Custom`], explicit fields are ignored; [`effective`](Self::effective)
resolves both to [`EffectivePolicy`].

capture_monitor.description:
Stream this physical connector (`DP-1`, `HDMI-A-2`) instead of a
virtual display; `None` is the virtual path. Host-wide, orthogonal
to `preset`. `PUNKTFUNK_CAPTURE_MONITOR` overrides it so `host.env`
can pin without a console write undoing it.

clients.description:
Per-device deviations, keyed by pairing fingerprint — what identity
slots, admission and the device list already key on (never an address:
a dual-boot box keeps its fingerprint and changes its IP).

Written only through `/display/clients/{fp}`; the host-wide PUT refuses
a `clients` key outright, so a stale console cannot round-trip the
whole map back over a change it never saw.

ddc_power_off.description:
Windows: DDC/CI panel off (VCP 0xD6) before Exclusive isolate, on at
restore. Cuts standby auto-input-scan / DP link churn on a dark
physical. Best-effort; no DDC/CI → skip. Orthogonal to `preset`; default off.

edid_lock.description:
Windows/AMD: pin connector EDID emulation while streaming
(`pf_win_display::adl_emul`). Locked at first Exclusive isolate
before physicals deactivate (awake sink answers the live-EDID read),
unlocked at last-member teardown, crash-journaled. Inert without
`atiadlxx.dll`. Orthogonal to `preset`; default off.

game_session.description:
Game-launch routing. Orthogonal to `preset`; `#[serde(default)]` is
`Auto` so older `display-settings.json` files stay untouched.

keep_monitors.description:
Connectors that stay lit while streaming, even under `exclusive`
(`design/web-console-overhaul.md` §5.5).

The shared-desktop case the all-or-nothing topology axis cannot express: the
couch TV streams on the sole screen while the desk monitor stays usable. Only
meaningful under `exclusive` — nothing else turns a monitor off.

launch_workspace.description:
Default for a launch whose library entry names no `on_window.workspace`.
Orthogonal to `preset`; `#[serde(default)]` is `own`, so an older
`display-settings.json` opts in with the rest.

max_displays.description: Simultaneous live virtual displays. Clamped to `1..=16` (connector ceiling).

pnp_disable_monitors.description:
Windows: disable the PnP nodes of the physical monitors the isolate
switched off, for the stream; re-enabled at teardown. Persistent so a
re-HPD stays off. Inactive externals are [`standby_sink_neutralise`]'s.
A crash journal re-enables leftovers. Orthogonal to `preset`; default
on, and a v1 file migrates to on.

version.description:
Schema version. Unknown versions load best-effort
([`DisplayPolicyStore::load_from`] warns) and write pins current.

DisplaySettingsState.description: Stored policy, preset expansions, effective policy, and which options this build enforces.

client_enforced.description:
Overlay fields this build acts on PER DEVICE. A strict subset of
`enforced`: an axis can be host-wide and not yet per-device, and the
console must not offer a device control the host would store and ignore
(`design/web-console-overhaul.md` D1).

clients.description:
Stored per-device overlays, so one fetch paints the device rows.
READ-ONLY here — writes go to `/display/clients/{fingerprint}`, and the
PUT below refuses a body carrying this key.

custom_presets.description: Saved custom presets (`display-presets.json`). Apply via a `Custom` policy of their fields.

enforced.description: Names this build acts on (live vs coming-soon). Per-backend nuance is on `/display/state`.

settings.description: Stored policy, or the built-in default when unconfigured.

EffectivePolicy.description:
The six axes after preset expansion. What lifecycle/registry read, and
what mgmt echoes as in-force.

Every field is required on the wire. This type is also
[`CustomPresetInput::fields`] (`POST/PUT /display/presets`) and a
response member three times. `#[serde(default)]` would turn
`{"name":"Kiosk","fields":{}}` into a 201 storing six unchosen axes and
make all six optional in OpenAPI. Catalog tolerance for older entries
lives on the read path only: [`StoredEffectivePolicy`].

app_id.description: Store-qualified id (`steam:570`); omit to end every waiting game.

streaming.description:
Also end `app_id` where it is on a live session, not only where it is
waiting out a reconnect window. Ignored without `app_id`.

EnvMarker.description:
Plugin-owned stores must name this on [`DetectHint`]; the host does not
read the launcher's files. Heroic's `HEROIC_APP_NAME` is the only signal
under Proton.

value.description: `None` matches key presence only — safe solely for one-game-at-a-time launchers.

summary.description: Every number the host has for the finished session, including why it ended.

oneOf.description: Fires once the host has seen the game process, not merely spawned its launcher.

Fires when the game's own window reaches the screen, which is often far
later than its process: a Proton prefix build, a splash on a black
window, an emulator loading a ROM.

app_id.description: Wayland `app_id` or X11 class; `steam_app_<id>` under gamescope; empty on Windows.

title.description: Title the compositor or the desktop reports for that window.

oneOf.description:
Explicit operator choice (`add_with_access(Some)`). A pairing with no choice
emits only `pairing.completed` — see `design/per-client-access.md`.

expires_unix.description: Host wall-clock unix seconds; absent = permanent.

oneOf.description: Post-pairing edit (console sheet / extend / expire-now), not the original grant.
Deadline fire on a live session. A device with no session expires silently.

backend.description: `VirtualDisplay::name` of the backend that minted it.

count.description: How many kept displays this release retired.

oneOf.description: Once per discovered version; a steady "newer exists" does not re-fire on every refresh.

install_kind.description: `apt`, `windows-installer`, … so a hook can hint how to update without a second call.

oneOf.description: Boot-time reconciliation by the NEW binary after a successful apply.

id.description: Plugin that registered, restarted, deregistered, or lease-expired. Re-read `GET /api/v1/plugins`.

oneOf.description: Payload-free: the store is a join. Re-read `GET /api/v1/store/catalog` / `…/installed`.
The operator changed host settings. Re-read `GET /api/v1/host/settings`.

Emitted on ACCEPT, and again if the executor later fails. A succeeded power
action ends this process, so "accepted with no later failure" is success.
Cert-lane invoker; absent for the operator console (admin lane).

id.description: `power.sleep`, `power.reboot`, `power.shutdown`, `host.restart`.

EventKind.description:
Internally tagged `"kind": "<domain>.<verb>"`, flattened into [`HostEvent`].
Additive-only within [`SCHEMA_VERSION`].

icon.description:
Brand-mark token (`steam`, `heroic`) — never bytes or a URL. See [`is_icon_token`].

The art proxy serves raster only ([`art::local_art_bytes`] refuses SVG as
script-capable XML), so the mark stays a name the client already ships.

id.description: Stable, store-qualified id: `steam:<appid>` or `custom:<id>`.

on_window.description:
Which workspace this title's windows open on, where the compositor can
place them ([`OnWindow`]).

provider.description:
Plugin that owns this entry. `None` only for operator-typed custom entries.
`GET /library?provider=` filters on it.

oneOf.description:
Play stats, once this host has launched the title (`stats.rs`). Joined at read
time from `library-stats.json`, never stored on the entry.

GameEntry.description: One title in the unified library, regardless of store.

GameMeta.description:
Optional display metadata, `#[serde(flatten)]`-ed into [`GameEntry`].

Values are free-form strings, not enums — emulation sources (RomM, EmuDeck,
Playnite) each have their own vocabulary and the host does not normalize it.

platform.description:
`"PS2"`, `"Xbox 360"`, `"SNES"`, … Installed-store scanners stamp `"PC"`;
`GET /library?platform=` filters on it (case-insensitive).

release_year.description: Year of first release — the granularity metadata sources agree on.

GameOnNewLaunch.description:
What to do with a title this client already has running when it launches a
**different** one.

A third axis, not a fourth [`GameOnSessionEnd`] value: that one is "this
session is over"; this one is "the player asked for something else". An
operator who wants a game to survive a disconnect can still want it closed
when they pick another title.

Scoped to this client's own launches, and only launches this host performed
([`crate::launchreg`]). A game the player started at the machine was never
recorded, so this cannot close it.

GameOnSessionEnd.description: What to do with the launched game when its session ends.

app.description: Store-qualified id (`steam:570`). Absent for an operator-typed GameStream `apps.json` command.

fingerprint.description: Stable id of the device that launched it; the filter handle a name cannot be.

GameRole.description:
Presentation hint: ordinary title vs the launcher itself (Steam Big Picture,
Heroic, Playnite fullscreen). A launcher entry launches, leases, and lists
like a game (design D4). Serde-default `game`; skipped when default so the
wire is unchanged for entries that don't opt in.

GameSession.description:
How a session that launches a game is served
(`design/gamemode-and-dedicated-sessions.md`). Top-level
[`DisplayPolicy`] field, not part of [`EffectivePolicy`], so a preset
never clobbers it. Linux-only in effect.

GameStats.description: One title's numbers. On the wire as `GameEntry.stats`; absent until the first launch.

last_played_unix_ms.description: Unix ms of the most recent launch. Stamped at launch, so a game just started sorts first.

last_run_ms.description: The run that started at `last_played_unix_ms`. Still growing while it runs.

encoder_pin.description:
`PUNKTFUNK_ENCODER` when pinned (`qsv` / `nvenc` / …, not `auto`). A vendor mismatch is
overridden at session open (adapter wins); the console uses this to flag a stale pin.

env_override.description: `PUNKTFUNK_RENDER_ADAPTER` when set. Honoured in `auto`; a manual pick overrides it.

preferred_id.description: Stored manual pick; retained in `auto` so the console can switch back. May name an absent GPU.

preferred_name.description: Label for the stored pick, kept even when that GPU is absent.

GyroCadence.description: Client gyro arrival counts. Absent when no pad ever sent motion.

stalls.description: Gaps of 500 ms or more — the feed stopping, not jitter.

debounce_ms.description: Minimum interval between firings, in milliseconds. 0 = fire every time.

oneOf.description: Exact-match constraints; every present field must match.

hmac_secret_file.description: HMAC secret file (`X-Punktfunk-Signature: sha256=<hex>`). Warns if world-readable.

on.description: Exact kind (`stream.started`) or `domain.*` prefix; same vocabulary as SSE `?kinds=`.

run.description: Detached shell command: event JSON on stdin, `PF_EVENT_*` env.

timeout_s.description: Exec timeout in seconds (1–600, default 30); the process group is killed on expiry.

HookFilter.description:
Exact-match filters on event identity fields. Absent fields do not constrain;
a field set on a kind that does not carry it (e.g. `client` on `host.started`) never matches.

client.description: Client/device name (`session.*`: the Dashboard's short client label).

HooksConfig.description: Operator hook config: `hooks.json` and the `/api/v1/hooks` body.

HostCheck.description: One health verdict — the wire shape.

id.description: Console i18n key. See [`ids`].

params.description: Interpolation for localized strings (`{user}`, `{group}`). Only the host can see these.

severity.description: Meaningless on `ok`/`inapplicable`; carried so the wire shape never changes as status flips.

since_unix.description: First non-ok observation this run. Per-run stamp, not a history.

summary.description: English fallback. Console localizes when it knows `id`.

seq.description: 1-based; a consumer resumes with `since = last seen`.

HostEvent.description: One lifecycle event as it appears on the wire (`data:` of one SSE frame).

HostFacts.description: The console greys out rows this host cannot install.

HostInfo.description: Host identity and capabilities. Static for the process except `local_ip`.

app_version.description: GameStream host version advertised to Moonlight clients.

codecs.description: Codecs this host can encode (`host_wire_caps`, not the compile-time list).

fingerprint.description:
Hex SHA-256 of this host's leaf certificate — what a client pins. Public by
construction: every client reads it off the handshake. Carried here so a connect link
can name it, and a first connect over an untrusted path is verified rather than blind.
`null` only if the identity could not be parsed.

gamestream.description: GameStream/Moonlight-compat planes are running (`--gamestream`). `false` is the default (native only).

gfe_version.description: GFE version advertised to Moonlight clients.

local_ip.description:
Fresh LAN IP each request — do not cache. Cold-boot and network-move report
`127.0.0.1` until a real address exists.

os.description:
OS chain, generic → specific, slash-separated (`windows` | `macos` |
`linux[/<family>][/<id>]`). Walk most-specific-first; an unknown distro still matches its family.

uniqueid.description: Persisted host id; pairing matches on this.

HostSettingsPatch.description: Setting id → new value; `null` returns a setting to its default.

env_file.description: The file an operator edits to pin a setting.

restart_pending.description: Setting ids waiting for a restart.

settings.description: Rows this host acts on, in page order.

HostTheme.description: The desktop's appearance, as far as this host can see it.

accent.description: `#rrggbb`, or `null` when the desktop has no accent to report.

mode.description: `light` | `dark`, or `null` when the desktop expresses no preference.

source.description:
Where the answer came from, for the console's "Follow host — Windows" line.
`null` when nothing answered.

Identity.description:
Stable identity so DEs persist per-display config (KDE scaling). Carried
as Windows EDID serial + IddCx connector index, KWin per-slot output
name, and the host-persisted Mutter scale map.

InputCounts.description:
Client datagrams this session took, by class.

Counted up to the moment the session was summarized: the reader task ends with the
connection, which closes after this, so a last straggler can fall outside.

dropped.description: Offers the input queue refused because it was full. Not a wire loss.

InstallRequest.description: Catalog `{source, id}` or a raw `spec` the operator owns.

accept_unverified.description:
Required with [`Self::spec`]. Without it the API refuses; a caller cannot skip the
unverified decision.

id.description: With [`Self::source`]: catalogued install.

spec.description:
Raw spec (`@scope/name`, `@scope/name@1.2.3`, https tarball or git+https). Nothing reviewed
it and nothing pins it.

blocked.description: Revocation of the installed version. Reported, never auto-removed.

tier.description: Install-time tier; unverified stays unverified after the dialog is gone.

update_available.description: Catalog version when newer than installed (a version string, not a bool).

Job.description: Snake_case matches the management API; index/sources/manifest files use npm camelCase.

oneOf.description:
Linger `seconds` after the last session leaves; a reconnect inside
the window reuses the display.

seconds.description:
Linger seconds, clamped to `0..=86400` on write. Longer is
`forever` in practice; unclamped `u32` is ~136 years and a
nonsense `expires_in_ms`.

oneOf.description:
Until host shutdown or `POST /display/release` (force-releases
`Pinned` like `Lingering`). The `gaming-rig` preset selects this.

KeepAlive.description:
Linger after the last client detaches. Tagged on `mode` so the web form
and OpenAPI stay `{"mode":"off"}` / `{"mode":"duration","seconds":N}` /
`{"mode":"forever"}`. On gamescope's bare spawn this also keeps the
nested session and its game.

name.description: The parameter's name in the template.

LaunchSpec.description:
How the host launches a title. Open-ended so new stores slot in:
`steam_appid` → `steam steam://rungameid/<value>`; `command` → run `<value>`
nested in a gamescope session.

args.description:
Values for an `exec` template's parameters. Each is checked against the character class
the manifest declares for it, and a path must sit inside the paths that manifest names.
A list rather than a map: a map of strings generates as an untyped object in the SDK.

value.description:
Appid for `steam_appid`, the shell command for `command`, or — for `exec` — the name of a
template in the publishing plugin's manifest.

positions.description:
Canonical decimal identity-slot ids (`"1"`..`"15"`) — the exact
string `arrange` looks up. [`DisplayPolicy::sanitized`] maps `"01"`
→ `"1"` and drops non-ids; a key that never matches is a pin the
console still shows while every session auto-rows past it.

LayoutMode.description:
Arrangement in desktop space. Computed only in `layout::arrange`:
`/display/state` and (Linux, KWin only) position apply both consume it.

LinkMinute.description:
One minute of link health for one session. Every field is a delta for the window except
the bands, which are min..max over it.

abr_backoffs.description:
Client bitrate asks below the rate the encoder was running. The host cannot see which
of loss, delay or decode drove them — only that the client's controller retreated.

anchor_p.description:
What the encoder answered an RFI with: a clean P against a surviving reference, or a
wave that recodes the picture over ~0.5 s.

egress_kbps.description: Sealed wire throughput over the window.

gaps.description: Pipeline gaps this host announced: its own stalls, not the network's.

keyframe_req.description: Client decode-recovery asks, and the IDRs actually forced (the cooldown coalesces).

loss_windows.description: Of `windows`, those that reported any loss.

retargets.description: Times the encoder's rate actually moved.

rfi.description:
Client reference-frame invalidation asks, and those the encoder refused (each refusal
costs an IDR).

secs.description: Seconds this line covers. 60, except the last line of a session.

session_id.description: The `/status` session id, so a line ties to a row.

unrecovered.description: Windows that closed with frames parity could not repair.

windows.description: Client loss reports that closed here. 0 = the client sent none, which is itself a fault.

LocalSummary.description:
Tray snapshot for loopback: counts, booleans, and `client_name`.
Unauthenticated; `require_auth` admits loopback only (the tray cannot read the bearer file).

audio_streaming.description: True while audio is streaming on either plane (same rule as `video_streaming`).

client_name.description: First native session's display name (trust-store, else connect-time). `null` when idle, nameless, or GameStream.

conflicts.description: Other GameStream hosts on this machine, detected at startup. Running one alongside is unsupported.

games.description: Compact labels (`Hades`, `Hades (closing in 4:12)`). Countdown means the client is gone and the host will end the game when the window closes.

kept_displays.description: Lingering or pinned virtual displays with no live session. Active (in-use) displays are not counted.

pending_approvals.description: Native pairing knocks awaiting the operator's approval (count only).

pin_pending.description: GameStream pairing is waiting for a PIN.

oneOf.description: GameStream launch if present, else the first live native session. `null` when idle.

video_streaming.description: Video streaming on either plane. The GameStream flag alone misses native sessions.

msg.description: Formatted message; structured fields appended as `key=value`.

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number (1-based) — pass the last one back as the `after` cursor.

dropped.description: Entries between `after` and the first returned one were already evicted.

next.description: Last returned seq, or the request's `after` when the page is empty.

ModeConflict.description:
Admission when a new client asks for a different mode than the live
display. [`super::admission`] runs this before Welcome so `reject` is a
handshake error, not a half-built session.

error.description: Enumeration failure. `None` with an empty list means the host has no heads.

monitors.description: Heads, ordered left-to-right by desktop position.

pin_supported.description:
True when this build can stream a chosen physical head.

Enumeration and capture are separate. Off Linux, heads are listed but there is no
mirror backend (`vdisplay::open` has no Windows arm; `pf-capture` only has
`open_idd_push`). The console treats `false` as a read-only picker.

pinned.description: Configured pin, even when it matches no head (console can show a dangling pin).

access_level.description:
`full` | `controller` | `view` | `custom`. Derived from `grants`;
absent only on hosts older than this field.

expires_unix.description:
Absolute expiry, unix seconds on the host clock. `null` = permanent.
An expired device stays listed; it is just not authorized.

fingerprint.description: Hex SHA-256 of the client certificate — the stable id.

granted_unix.description: Last grant time, unix seconds. Display/audit only; never enforced.

grants.description: `GRANT_*` bits 0–5. `null` is a pre-grants record, which means full.

preferred_pad_slot.description:
Player slot this device's pads take, 0-based; `null` = whichever comes free.
Set through `PUT /session/{id}/player` while the device streams.

until_disconnect.description:
The record is dropped when the device's last session ends, rather than at a clock
time. `expires_unix` may also be set; whichever comes first ends the grant.

NativePairStatus.description:
Native pairing window. Unlike GameStream, the host mints the PIN (SPAKE2
needs it client-side first); the console displays it.

enabled.description: True when this process started with `--native`.

expires_in_secs.description: Seconds left in the window. `null` if disarmed, or armed with no expiry (CLI flag).

OnWindow.description:
Per-entry window placement, applied once when the game's own window first
reaches the screen. Absent keys take the defaults below; `workspace` alone
falls back to the host's `launch_workspace` display policy.

focus.description:
Raise it. Default on: the player launched it, so it is what they want
in front — a launcher that steals focus back leaves them on the desk.

fullscreen.description:
Make it full-screen. Default off: most games set their own mode, and
forcing it fights a title that wanted a window.

move_to_stream_output.description:
Move it onto the streamed head if it opened elsewhere. Default on: a
game the player cannot see is the whole failure this stage exists for.

hidden.description: Set by [`set_entry_hidden`]. Omitted when false so the shape only grows for hidden titles.

OperatorGameEntry.description:
A library entry plus the operator's view of it — whether they hid it.

A field on [`GameEntry`] would leak onto every lane: `GET /library` returns
`Vec<GameEntry>` except on the operator's lane, so a hidden flag cannot
reach a paired client. `flatten` keeps the wire a plain entry plus one key.

PadFrame.description:
One pad's whole state as the host holds it — the `data:` of one SSE frame.

Whole state, not a delta: a page that attaches mid-press draws what is held without
replaying history, and the console derives its event log by diffing consecutive frames.

declared.description:
What the client declared at arrival, when it declared one. Differs from `device`
where the build cannot construct that kind and folded it into one it can.

device.description: The virtual controller the host built: `xbox360`, `dualsense`, `steamdeck`, …

pad.description: Wire index — the number this client gave the pad.

present.description: `false` is the unplug frame: the host holds no device at this index any more.

slot.description:
Host-wide OS slot — the identity every per-pad host resource is named by
(mailbox, `SwDeviceCreate` instance, pairing MAC). Absent before the first
frame builds the device.

fingerprint.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the client certificate DER — the client's stable id here.

label.description:
Operator-assigned display name (`PATCH /clients/{fp}`). The only way to tell two
paired Moonlight devices apart; absent until somebody names the device.

subject.description:
Certificate subject if the DER parses. Do not display as a device name: every
moonlight-common-c client self-signs `CN=NVIDIA GameStream Client`, so this names
the protocol. [`Self::label`] is the field to show.

pending.description:
Parked ceremonies. Echo this identity in the submit so the PIN addresses the
ceremony the operator saw, not a later arrival.

PendingCeremony.description: One pairing handshake parked waiting for its PIN.

PendingDevice.description: Knock awaiting delegated approval (pair here instead of fetching a PIN).

access_level.description:
Stored mask's preset. `null` with no stored record — unlike
[`NativeClient`], where it is always derivable.

expires_unix.description:
Stored absolute expiry (unix seconds; often already past). `null` if
unknown or permanent.

fingerprint.description: Hex SHA-256 of the device certificate — what approval pins.

granted_unix.description: Stored grant time, unix seconds. `null` if unknown.

grants.description:
Stored mask if this fingerprint was paired before (expired-guest
re-knock). `null` if unknown, or a pre-grants record (= full).

id.description: Approve/deny id. Per-process; entries expire after ~10 minutes.

source.description:
Where the knock came from: `"lan"` or `"wan"`. A `"wan"` device cannot be admitted by
approve — arm a PIN bound to its fingerprint instead.

until_disconnect.description: Stored "this session" setting if this fingerprint was paired before. `false` if unknown.

Plane.description: Origin plane. Both planes must emit; filtering is the consumer's job.

apps.description: Lowercased app names, as the voice-chat app list matches them.

category.description:
Plugin kind, not a UI field. Console hides `library` from the nav (those plugins already have
Game sources); omit the field to keep a nav page.

oneOf.description: Absent `ui` is a live listing with no nav entry — not an error.

PluginSummary.description: Listing row. Never carries the secret — the browser reaches the UI only through the console proxy.

PluginUi.description: Request body only — carries the secret. [`PluginUiPublic`] is the response view.

port.description: Loopback only — the host dials `127.0.0.1:<port>`; a registration cannot carry a hostname.

secret.description: Per-boot; the console proxy presents it as `Authorization: Bearer`. Rotated on plugin restart.

PluginUiPublic.description: Secret-free UI view for the listing. The secret never goes here.

PortMap.description: Ports a client needs. Moonlight derives stream ports from HTTP; a control pane should not.

PrepCmd.description:
Per-app prep (Sunshine `prep-cmd` parity): `do` runs synchronously before launch;
`undo` runs at session end, reverse order, best-effort, including panic-unwind ([`PrepGuard`]).

do.description: Command run before launch. Same recipe and ownership checks as hook `run`; stdin is `{}`.

undo.description: After session end. Skipped when its `do` failed (it never took effect).

Preset.description:
Named bundle of the fields below. `Custom` uses the explicit fields;
any other preset ignores them and expands ([`DisplayPolicy::effective`]).

PresetInfo.description: Picker row. `fields` is the expansion so the console does not hardcode it.

id.description: `default` | `gaming-rig` | `shared-desktop` | `hotdesk` | `workstation`.

detect.description: Install-dir / process hint. Needed when launch goes through the provider's own client.

icon.description: Brand token a plugin sets on its `launchers(cfg)` tiles. See [`GameEntry::icon`].

on_window.description: Which workspace the title opens on; absent follows the host's display policy.

prep.description: Run as the host user; operator-privileged. See [`privileged_field`].

ProviderEntryInput.description: One title in a provider reconcile payload: [`CustomInput`] plus the provider's required stable key.

ttl_s.description: Seconds this report stays authoritative without being restated.

unknown.description: Ignored because no such entry exists (report raced a reconcile).

running.description: Complete running set, not a delta: anything absent is reported as stopped.

sessions.description:
Newest first. Bounded in memory and lost on a host restart — this is the last
few sessions, not a history.

slot.description: Slot to release (see `state`); omit to release **all** kept displays.

Remedy.description:
Operator action. Copy-paste only: the host is unprivileged and does not run the command.
Joining `punktfunk` is opt-in — write on the vhci `attach` node materialises arbitrary USB.

relogin_required.description: Fix takes effect only after logout. `systemd --user` keeps the group set it started with.

text.description: English fallback. The console overrides it by check id.

RenameClient.description: Body of `PATCH /clients/{fingerprint}` — the device's display name.

label.description:
Display name. `null` or empty/whitespace clears it (listed by fingerprint alone).

Scrubbed with the native-plane sanitizer: control characters and Unicode bidi
overrides stripped (one device could impersonate another in this list), whitespace
collapsed, capped at 64 characters.

external_id.description: Same key the reconcile payload uses.

pid.description:
Pid the provider started, when it knows one. Re-resolved and pinned to start time
before any signal; a stale or recycled pid contributes nothing.

RuntimeStatus.description: Live status; changes as sessions start and end.

active_sessions.description:
Live sessions on both planes. Native admits concurrent sessions so this can exceed 1;
`session`/`stream` are one representative and `sessions` is the list.

oneOf.description: Windows audio-wiring verdict; absent off-Windows and before the first pass. Present while idle.
Windows display state: topology transactions and outstanding device leases. Absent off-Windows.

games.description: Launched titles: live sessions plus `state: "grace"` reconnect-window rows. Empty for a desktop-only stream.

paired_clients.description: GameStream paired-cert count. Native devices are `native_paired_clients`; sum both for the total.

pin_pending.description: Pairing handshake is waiting for a PIN (`POST /api/v1/pair/pin`).

oneOf.description:
GameStream launch if present, else the first live native session. `null` when idle.
`session_id` says which row of `sessions` this is.

session_id.description:
Which `sessions` row `session`/`stream` describe. `null` when idle, or when the
representative is the GameStream stream (the compat plane has no id).

sessions.description: Every live session, one row each — what the per-session routes take an id from.

oneOf.description: Active stream parameters of that same session. `null` when idle.

principal.description: Windows: the account the task runs as.

ScannerInfo.description: One game source and its enable state — the console toggle row.

entries.description: Titles this source currently contributes. `None` on `Builtin` (counting would walk launcher files).

id.description:
Entry `store`, provider id, and store claim. One string, so a disabled
toggle survives the store's plugin taking over.

origin.description: Always `plugin` on this host. `Builtin` remains so OpenAPI still names it for N-1 consoles.

provider.description: Provider id. `None` only for a `Builtin` source an N-1 host still reports.

grants.description: What now governs the session — the request ANDed with the pairing's mask.
Exact `GRANT_*` mask, for a level the three names do not cover. Reserved bits are 400.

muted.description: `true` stops audio leaving for this session.

SessionEndReason.description:
Why a session ended, in the client's own words
([`punktfunk_core::client::PunktfunkEndReason`]) so both ends name the same end the
same way. The bytes match that ABI where the two overlap.

[`Self::StoppedByOperator`] is the one a client cannot see: the host closes it as
code 0, which every client reads as `host_ended`.

oneOf.description:
Live capture health (Windows IDD-push, native plane). Absent on GameStream, on Linux,
and until the video loop's first publish.

pads.description:
OS pad slots the session holds right now. A pad already built keeps its slot
until it re-plugs, so this can still name the old player for a moment.

reserved.description:
`false` = another live session asked for that slot first and keeps it; this
session stays on the first-free claim.

slot.description: The pick now stored for this session.

Player slot, 0-based: `0` is Player 1. Omit or `null` to hand the session
back to the first-free claim.

SessionRef.description: Plane-neutral A/V session (distinct from a video [`StreamRef`]).

client.description: Cert-fingerprint prefix, or peer IP for an anonymous client — not [`ClientRef::name`].

fingerprint.description: The device's full stable id, for a hook filter. Absent for an anonymous client.

plane.description: Which plane serves it, as `stream.*` and `game.*` also report.

SessionRow.description:
One live session as the Dashboard lists it: who, where, since when, and the state
the per-session routes change.

access_level.description:
`full` | `controller` | `view` | `custom`, live — not the pairing's stored level.
`null` on the compat plane, which is ungoverned.

client.description: Fingerprint prefix, or peer IP for an anonymous client.

client_name.description: Display name (trust store, else the name the client sent). `null` if nameless.

id.description:
Pass to `DELETE /session/{id}` and friends. `null` on the compat plane, which
has no per-session handle — stop it with the host-wide `DELETE /session`.

join.description:
Sharing another session's display rather than owning one. Which session it joined
is not reported yet — the two registries do not share ids (issue #1095).

oneOf.description:
The last closed minute of link health: loss, the recovery frames it cost, and the FEC
and bitrate bands. `null` in a session's first minute, and on the compat plane.

muted.description: Audio is held back for this session alone (`PUT /session/{id}/audio`).

pads.description:
OS pad slots this session holds, lowest first. Slot `n` is player `n + 1` to a
local co-op game. Empty while the session has no controller.

preferred_pad_slot.description:
Player slot the operator picked for this session, 0-based (`PUT
/session/{id}/player`). `null` = the slot is whichever comes free.

shared_path_with.description:
Other live sessions from this client's address — one NAT or tunnel, so most likely one
network path. Their bitrates adapt independently. Absent when there are none.

enforced.description:
Axes this build enforces. Empty with no launch path (macOS) so the console
does not offer a no-op switch.

SessionSummary.description:
Everything the host knows about one finished session.

The `session.ended` payload AND the body of `GET /api/v1/session/last`: one struct,
so a screenshot of the console card is the API answer a bug report would have carried.
A number the host does not accumulate per session is absent rather than zero.

oneOf.description: Absent when the session ran no audio plane (synthetic source, or the thread never started).

bit_depth.description: 8 or 10. Independent of `hdr` — 10-bit SDR is a mode.

oneOf.description: What the encoder's target did. Absent on a session that opened no encoder.

bitrate_kbps.description: The encoder's target when the session ended, kbps. `bitrate` has the span.

bringup_ms.description: Hello → first video packet, ms. `0` if no packet ever left.

client.description: Cert-fingerprint prefix, or peer IP for an anonymous client.

client_name.description: Display name (trust store, else the name the client sent). Absent if nameless.

frames_dropped.description:
Frames the capturer's encode pool refused. Absent on a capturer that does not
count them (everything but the Windows IDD push path).

frames_sent.description:
Access units the send thread put on the wire. Absent when the video loop
never reached its tail — the `host_error` case.

oneOf.description: Absent when no pad sent motion — most sessions.

id.description: Same id [`SessionRef`] and the per-session routes carry.

join.description: Shared another session's display at ITS mode instead of owning one.

mode.description: `WxH@Hz` as last delivered; a mid-session mode switch moves it.

path_mtu.description: Path MTU the QUIC stack settled on, bytes. Absent as `frames_sent` is.

started_unix.description: Host wall clock at stream start, unix seconds.

gpu_id.description: Required for `manual`: a currently listed GPU `id`.

mode.description: `auto` (env pin, else max dedicated VRAM) or `manual`.

SettingState.description: One setting as the console renders it.

env.description: The name to set in `host.env` to pin this setting.

id.description: Store key; the console's copy key is `setting_<id>`.

options.description: `enum` only, canonical spellings in display order.

origin.description: The env var or CLI flag that set `value` (`source` `env` or `flag`).

restart_pending.description: Changed since the host started, and applies only after a restart.

stored.description: The console's value, even while an env var or flag overrides it.

title.description: English label, for a setting the console has no copy for.

Severity.description:
Weight of a non-ok status. Orthogonal to [`CheckStatus`]: a check can `warn` about something
`critical` (degraded, not dead). The console sorts by both.

public_key.description: `ed25519:<base64>`. Omitted ⇒ an unsigned source (accepted, flagged everywhere).

SourceOrigin.description: Origin of a [`ScannerInfo`]. This host emits only `Plugin`.

builtin.description: Built-in `unom`: not editable, not removable; only its entries may be `verified`.

fetched_at.description: Unix seconds of the cached index, if any.

signed.description: Unsigned sources still serve; the console flags them.

stale.description: Last refresh missed; entries still install — the pin travelled with the entry.

StageTiming.description: One stage's p50/p99 in an aggregation window (microseconds).

name.description:
Pipeline order, named per path. Linux native: `queue capture submit encode send`.
Windows driver: `pool encode ipc copy send`, or `driver copy send` from a driver that
does not stamp its slots. GameStream: `capture encode packetize send send_spread`, with
the same two driver sets on Windows.

StatsSample.description: One aggregated sample (~2 s native, ~1 s GameStream).

fec_recovered.description: FEC shards the receiver recovered. Only a client measures it.

fec_us.description:
Sealing one frame, mean µs over the window: FEC parity, AES-GCM, the socket sends.
Native only; timed while a capture runs.

fps.description: Genuine new frames/s from the source (not including repeats).

frames_dropped.description:
Counters are deltas for this window. `None` = this path cannot see it, never a zero it
did not measure. Frames the host dropped: the driver's pool, or GameStream's queue.

host_p50_us.description: Capture → fully sent, p50/p99 µs: the span a client's `host` term reports.

mbps.description:
Attempted sealed wire Mb/s at seal time (AU + shard framing + FEC, including
datagram-aligned zero-pad). Not goodput; socket send drops do not reduce it.

packets_dropped.description: Receiver-side loss. Only a client measures it; recordings older than this field hold 0.

repeat_fps.description: Re-encoded holds/s — source starvation, not new frames.

rtt_us.description: Smoothed QUIC round trip to the client, µs.

session_id.description: Distinguishes concurrent sessions (usually constant for one loop).

t_ms.description: Milliseconds since capture start (monotonic; stamped by [`StatsRecorder::push_sample`]).

StatsStatus.description: In-progress capture, as the management API reports it.

elapsed_ms.description:
Host monotonic elapsed ms (`0` if idle). Do not subtract `started_unix_ms`
from the console's wall clock — that clock may be skewed.

started_unix_ms.description: Unix start of the in-progress capture (`0` if idle).

StreamInfo.description: Negotiated stream parameters (RTSP on GameStream; live mode on native).

last_resize_ms.description: Last mid-stream resize, reconfigure → rebuilt, ms. Native only; `null` if none / GameStream.

min_fec.description: Client's parity floor per FEC block (`minRequiredFecPackets`).

time_to_first_frame_ms.description: Hello → first video packet, ms. Native only; `null` on GameStream or while still bringing up.

StreamRef.description: Live video stream (what the stream marker file reflects).

app.description: Store-qualified id on the native plane, app title on GameStream.

fingerprint.description:
The device's stable id — what a hook filter should key on, since a display name is
neither unique nor fixed. Absent for an anonymous client.

SubmitPin.description: PIN plus the exact ceremony selected from `GET /pair`.

label.description:
Name for this device, scrubbed like `PATCH /clients/{fp}` and stored once the pairing
completes. Every Moonlight client names itself the same, so without one the device is
listed by fingerprint until somebody renames it.

fingerprint.description: The device's own fingerprint, so a client can show which identity it is using.

device_key.description:
Base64 SPKI of the device's P-256 public key — the same bytes it paired with, whose
SHA-256 the host stored.

signature.description:
Base64 ECDSA-P256-SHA256 signature, ASN.1 DER, over the same message the control stream
uses: context, the host's identity fingerprint, then the nonce.

Toplevel.description:
One compositor toplevel, as every backend reports it.

`id` is the backend's own handle (a Hyprland address, a sway con id) and is
opaque above this module: it goes back to the backend that minted it and
nowhere else. Defined on every platform — the management route and its
schema exist on a Windows host too, which simply lists nothing.

app_id.description: Wayland `app_id`, or the X11 class on an Xwayland window.

id.description: Backend handle. Never parsed above the backend, never reused across one.

output.description: The head this window is on — always the streamed one, by construction.

pid.description: `None` where the compositor does not report one (some Xwayland cons).

workspace.description: Workspace name as the compositor spells it, not its id.

Topology.description: Host topology while managed virtual displays are up.

TopologyTransaction.description: One topology transaction as the display actor recorded it.

UiCredential.description: The only shape that returns a secret. The console BFF denylists this lookup from the browser.

UnpairAllResult.description:
Bulk-unpair result, shared by `/clients` and `/native/clients`.

A count, not 204: unpair-everything is idempotent, and the operator still
needs to know whether that was three devices or none.

UpdateJobInfo.description: In-process apply, or a leftover installer that has not resolved yet.

stale.description: Last verified manifest older than 45 days.

UpdateNativeAccess.description:
Partial PATCH of a paired device's grants/expiry. Omitted fields keep their
current value.

clear_expiry.description: `true` makes access permanent. Mutually exclusive with `expires_in_secs` (400).

expires_in_secs.description:
New expiry from now, seconds. `0` expires now. Omit to keep current.
Mutually exclusive with `clear_expiry` (400).

grants.description: New `GRANT_*` mask; reserved bits are 400. Omit to keep current grants.

until_disconnect.description: Drop the record once the device's last session ends. Omit to keep the current setting.

UpdateResultInfo.description: Last apply outcome. Survives the host's own restart.

staged.description: Applied; activates on the next reboot (rpm-ostree).

available.description: Newer than `current_version` on this channel. Unparseable pairs never flag.

channel_hint.description: Copy-paste update command for this install kind.

not_published.description:
Feed 404 for this channel: nothing published yet, not a check failure.
Mutually exclusive with `last_error`. Never set once a manifest has been
seen — a feed that then 404s is an error.

opt_in_hint.description:
One-click apply is possible but not opted in — command to run
(Linux: join `punktfunk-update`).

allow_pooling.description:
`allowPooling: true` is a `TypeError` when combined with `serverCertificateHashes`, so a
client must pass this. Stated here because a browser that ignores it fails at Web PKI
validation with no useful error.

cert_hash_sha256.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the leaf certificate DER — the bytes that go in
`serverCertificateHashes[0].value`.

cert_hash_sig.description:
Hex ECDSA-P256-SHA256 signature (ASN.1 DER) by the host's long-lived native identity over
`"punktfunk-wt-cert-v1:" + cert_hash_sha256`. Absent when that identity is the legacy RSA
pair. A browser that has paired MUST check this; one that has not cannot, and does not.

expires_at.description:
Unix seconds. Past this the certificate has rotated and the hash above is stale; fetch
again rather than cache. Always under two weeks out — the spec refuses anything longer.

host_cert_der.description:
Base64 DER of the native identity's leaf certificate — the key that verifies
`cert_hash_sig`. A browser hashes it and compares with the fingerprint it stored at
pairing; trusting it without that check would defeat the whole exercise.

port.description: UDP port the plane listens on. Not the management port, and not the native plane's.

WindowVerb.description:
What a client may ask of one window.

Defined on every platform: the management route decodes it before any
backend is consulted.

WorkspacePlacement.description:
Where a library launch's windows open on the streamed head.

Default `own`: the player gets the game on an empty workspace instead of
the operator's desk. Honoured only by the backends that can place a launch
(`claim_workspace`); everywhere else a launch is always `current`.

[`DisplayPolicy`] field, not part of [`EffectivePolicy`]: a preset never
clobbers it. A library entry's own `on_window.workspace` outranks it.
